lesson_title: The Running Total Tells a Different Story
hook_text: One curve, one ruler, two moves — and the median, quartiles and percentiles all fall out. Meet the ogive.
clip_script: Fifty learners logged their daily study time. Want the median without touching a calculator? There's a curve for that — the ogive — and it runs on tuckshop logic. A tuckshop owner keeps two columns: what came in TODAY, and the total SO FAR. The histogram is the today column — how many in each class. The ogive is the so-far column: four, thirteen, thirty, forty-two, fifty. Plot each total at the END of its class — because thirteen-under-thirty is only true at thirty — start at zero-zero, and join the dots. You get a lazy-S that climbs fast where the data crowds, and NEVER comes downhill, because running totals don't shrink. Now the magic: two ruler moves answer everything. Median? Go ACROSS from position twenty-five, then DOWN: about forty-one minutes. Quartiles? Across from twelve and a half, and from thirty-seven and a half: about twenty-nine and fifty-four. Ninetieth percentile? Across from forty-five: about sixty-six. How many study more than fifty-five minutes? Go UP from fifty-five, read about thirty-eight below, subtract from fifty — about twelve. One curve, one ruler, every position question. Just say the magic word: approximately.
visual_style: A tuckshop notebook morphs into a climbing lazy-S curve on graph paper; a glowing ruler slides across and down leaving dotted trails, and each reading stamps its answer with an 'approximately' tag.
pacing: Quick tuckshop setup, rhythmic build of the running totals, smooth S-curve reveal, rapid-fire across-and-down readings.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read medians straight off the graph.
